topIssues.title: prod: agent provisioning regressed to 16% failure on 2026-08-06 after eleven clean days
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Symptom

Agent creation started failing on 2026-08-06, after eleven consecutive clean days, and has not recovered.

By job finalisation day (`jobs` where `type='agent_provision'`, production):

```
2026-07-29 → 2026-08-05     0 failures across 63 jobs
2026-08-06 onward           20 failed / 124 jobs over the trailing 7 days = 16.1% hard failure
```

This is a dated regression, not background noise. The eleven-day clean streak immediately before it is what makes the break legible.

## What the user experiences

The happy path is fast — **66 s p50** from message to a running container. The failure path is not: retries and the job watchdog mean roughly **52 minutes** elapse before the user is told anything went wrong, and what they are told then sends them to a control panel.

Worse, until #17924 lands, each of these failures converts into a *permanent* lockout: the resulting `error` row blocks that organization from ever provisioning again through the onboarding chat. That is the mechanism behind the population in that issue growing from 60 to 69 in fifteen hours.

## Where to start

Three candidate contributors are already known and measured; this issue is to establish which of them accounts for the 16%, and whether there is a fourth:

1. **Fleet capacity.** 193 counted slots against 168 declared, four nodes over their ceiling, and **3 free slots** across the whole fleet (#17866). Placement funnels onto whichever node has room, which is how the 2026-08-06/07 outage happened (#17880).
2. **The proactive autoscaler cannot add nodes.** `evaluateCapacity` gates scale-up on `enabled.length < maxNodes` with `maxNodes` hardcoded to **12** (`node-autoscaler.ts:65`, no env override) against **14 enabled** — so it can only drain. On-demand autoscale during a provision still works (a node cold-started in 58 s on 08-08), but nothing pre-warms.
3. **The replacement-cleanup fence deadlock** (#17924 comment): fences accrue 3 → 4 → 6 over 06/07/08 Aug and are never retired, and a stranded fence makes the enqueue refuse with 409.

Note the daemon running production provisioning is currently pinned well behind `main`, so fixes already merged for this area are not in effect there.

## Suggested acceptance

Failure rate back under 1% over a rolling 7 days, and the time-to-user-notification on the failure path brought down from ~52 minutes to something a person will wait through.

Related: #17866, #17880, #17924.

[stan-cloud]

topIssues.title: auth: /steward/auth/providers gates the sign-in buttons for up to 4.7s in production
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Symptom

On the sign-in screen — the first thing anyone sees — the page paints almost instantly but the user cannot act for up to **4.7 seconds on production**. "Loading sign-in options…" stays on screen the whole time.

## Measurement

Browser timing on `app-staging.elizacloud.ai/login`:

```
first-contentful-paint    92 ms
load complete            153 ms
/steward/auth/providers  1242 ms      <- the only resource over 400 ms
```

`curl`, five consecutive runs per environment:

```
/steward/auth/providers   staging: 3.53  0.78  0.79  0.74  2.75  s
                          PROD:    3.71  0.78  0.76  0.75  4.69  s

/api/health (same Worker) staging: 0.087 s        PROD: 0.065 s
```

So the endpoint is roughly **10× slower warm** and **up to 60× slower cold** than a neighbouring route on the same Worker. Production is consistently the worse of the two.

## Why this one endpoint gates everything

The sign-in buttons (passkey, magic link, Google/Discord/GitHub, EVM/Solana) are all rendered from this response, so its latency is the user's time-to-first-action. Everything else on the page is already there at 92 ms.

## What to look at

The shape of the numbers — a fast floor around 750 ms with occasional multi-second spikes — reads like a per-request upstream call with no caching, plus a cold-start path. Worth establishing before fixing:

1. Is this served by the cloud Worker directly or proxied to a Steward backend? If proxied, the 750 ms floor is probably the upstream round trip.
2. Is the provider list effectively static? The set of enabled auth providers changes at deploy/config time, not per request — if so it is cacheable with a generous TTL, and the spikes disappear with the cold path.
3. If a cache layer already exists here, check whether it is actually enabled in each environment before adding another.

Whatever the remedy, state explicitly what could go stale and how a provider change propagates — silently serving a removed provider on a login screen is worse than the latency.

## Suggested acceptance

Time-to-interactive on the login screen under ~300 ms at p95, in production, measured the same way as above.

Found during a QA pass of the app surfaces.

[stan-cloud]

topIssues.title: Post-merge #18079: Unicode sanitizer misses request fields and JSON keys
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Post-merge regression

#18079 was merged to develop as 6160885f561f2f38023d37d73315ef5929c5a4e3. Re-auditing that exact merged tree confirms the remaining blockers from its exact head b607317fcb7e726e7df29e429ba0b5f7bc83ff14. The five relevant files are byte-identical between those commits.

## Deterministic evidence at 6160885

1. JSON object keys are not sanitized.

packages/core/src/utils/well-formed.ts:142-147 recursively sanitizes each entry value, then reuses the original key. The exact merged helper produces:

    deepToWellFormedUnicode({ ["bad\uD83D"]: "ok" })
    JSON.stringify(...) === '{"bad\\ud83d":"ok"}'

2. An own __proto__ key is corrupted when any sibling changes.

The clone is a normal object and writes next[key] = sanitized. With:

    JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"marker":"kept"},"bad":"\\ud83d"}')

the input has an own __proto__ property, but the sanitized result does not; serialization becomes {"bad":"�"}. The assignment mutates the clone prototype instead of preserving the JSON member.

3. The provider boundary still does not sanitize the whole request.

- plugins/plugin-openai/models/text.ts:2029-2041 sanitizes prompt/messages and system, then appends raw tools, toolChoice, output, and providerOptions.
- plugins/plugin-anthropic/models/text.ts:1329-1350 does the same and also appends raw stopSequences.

A lone surrogate in an Anthropic stop sequence, or in an OpenAI/Anthropic tool description/schema, therefore still reaches captured request JSON as a \ud8xx escape. This contradicts the merged comment that every outgoing string is forced well-formed.

4. Surrogate-safe truncation reports the wrong dropped count.

At packages/core/src/runtime/planner-rendering.ts:79-90 and packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts:2279-2281, the marker count is computed from requested head/tail lengths before the helpers back off at surrogate boundaries. Exact repro:

    input = "💀".repeat(100) // 200 UTF-16 code units
    truncateToolResultText(input, 30)
    => "💀💀 [193 chars truncated] 💀"

The output preserves 6 code units, so 6 + 193 = 199, not 200.

## Release impact

#18028 currently points at the same merged commit 6160885 and therefore contains these defects. It should not be promoted until this issue is fixed and the release gates are green.

## Required fix/coverage

- Sanitize the complete JSON-shaped request immediately before each SDK call, including tools, tool choice, output/schema, provider options, and stop sequences.
- Sanitize object keys with a defined collision policy and preserve own JSON members such as __proto__ safely, for example with a null-prototype clone plus defineProperty.
- Compute truncation markers from the actual retained code-unit lengths.
- Add loopback wire tests for tool descriptions/schemas and Anthropic stop sequences, plus unit tests for malformed keys, __proto__, and an astral-only exact count invariant.

topIssues.author: standujar

## Contribution provenance

- Client / agent tooling: Codex

**Describe the bug**

The secret-backed `App Live E2E` Cloud job is now a real, non-vacuous test, but it silently exercises the production Cloud API. There is still no authenticated lane proving the requested staging path: `app-staging.elizacloud.ai` / `api-staging.elizacloud.ai` auth handoff, agent selection/provisioning, and a real chat reply.

The latest scheduled control, [run 31246054455 / job 93074733709](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/31246054455/job/93074733709), executed the one Cloud test and passed in 38.3 seconds. That is useful production evidence, but it is not staging evidence:

- `.github/workflows/app-live-e2e.yml` sets `ELIZA_UI_SMOKE_CLOUD_LIVE` and a repository Cloud key, but does not set `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_BASE_URL`, select an environment, or assert the resolved host.
- `packages/ui/src/cloud/lib/api-client.ts` defaults direct Cloud traffic to `https://api.elizacloud.ai`.
- `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/cloud-live.spec.ts` drives a locally built renderer, not the deployed `app-staging.elizacloud.ai` artifact.
- The current names-only GitHub `staging` Environment secret inventory has neither `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` nor `ELIZACLOUD_API_KEY`, so there is no proven staging-scoped test credential route today.

This lets a green production-default job look like coverage for staging while the staging first-run path remains unproved.

**To Reproduce**

1. Inspect the `cloud-live` job environment in `.github/workflows/app-live-e2e.yml`; there is no Cloud base/environment override.
2. Inspect `DEFAULT_DIRECT_CLOUD_API_BASE_URL` in `packages/ui/src/cloud/lib/api-client.ts`; it is the production API.
3. Inspect the latest successful Cloud job log: one real login/provision/chat test passes, but no exact staging target is selected or asserted.
4. List GitHub staging Environment secret names only; no staging-scoped Cloud API credential is present under either accepted name.

**Expected behavior**

- A secret-gated staging lane uses a staging-scoped credential and fails closed unless the exact API origin is `https://api-staging.elizacloud.ai`.
- It proves auth return, agent selection/provisioning in under 60 seconds, and a real non-stub reply with measured first-turn latency.
- It identifies whether it tested the deployed `app-staging.elizacloud.ai` artifact or a local renderer; both contracts must not be conflated.
- It defaults to a shared/reusable QA agent and has explicit cleanup/reuse semantics. Dedicated provisioning remains separately opt-in because it can create billable resources.
- Production and staging results are reported as separate jobs/artifacts, never inferred from one another.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

topIssues.title: [staging][CI] Release PR previews overwrite the canonical develop Pages branch while API deploy is skipped
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Contribution provenance

AI assistance is self-reported provenance, not a request for hidden reasoning.
Use the exact runtime values; do not include secrets, tokens, private prompts,
session IDs, or chain-of-thought.

- AI assistance: yes
- AI provider/model: OpenAI / gpt-5.6-sol
- Client / agent tooling: Codex
- Contribution skill revision: N/A - contribute-to-eliza skill was not available
- Attribution status: self-reported

**Describe the bug**

Pull-request Pages previews use `github.head_ref` verbatim as the Cloudflare Pages branch. A release PR whose head branch is the canonical `develop` branch therefore deploys its preview bundle to the real `develop` Pages alias used by the staging custom domains.

The same pull-request run intentionally skips database migrations and the API Worker, so it can update both staging frontends while leaving the staging API on an older commit. This creates an unverified frontend/API combination on `staging.elizacloud.ai` and `app-staging.elizacloud.ai`; auth, provisioning, or chat contracts can change on only one side.

Current source has the collision in both Pages jobs:

- console branch resolver: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/ba0dc76f86561ba1642255193ab1217b2b013e8b/.github/workflows/cloud-cf-deploy.yml#L1262-L1277
- app branch resolver: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/ba0dc76f86561ba1642255193ab1217b2b013e8b/.github/workflows/cloud-cf-deploy.yml#L1657-L1672

**To Reproduce**

1. Open or synchronize a pull request from `develop` into `main` that touches a Cloud CF workflow path.
2. Observe the `Cloud CF Deploy` pull-request run.
3. `Run Database Migrations` and `Deploy API Worker` are skipped, as designed for previews.
4. Both Pages jobs resolve `PR_HEAD_REF=develop`, then invoke Wrangler with `PAGES_BRANCH=develop`.
5. Observe that the canonical staging Pages manifests advance while `https://api-staging.elizacloud.ai/api/health` does not.

Exact reproduction: release PR run https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/31276896449

- event: `pull_request`
- head: `develop@ba0dc76f86561ba1642255193ab1217b2b013e8b`
- migrations: skipped
- API Worker: skipped
- console Pages: success, alias `develop.eliza-cloud-enq.pages.dev`
- app Pages: success, alias `develop.eliza-app.pages.dev`

Job logs:

- console: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/31276896449/job/93152528322
- app: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/31276896449/job/93152528329

**Expected behavior**

- Every pull request uses a collision-resistant preview branch derived from the PR number or another immutable PR identity, including the special `develop → main` release PR.
- A pull-request event must fail closed if its resolved Pages branch equals a canonical branch such as `main` or `develop`.
- Only a canonical push/manual staging release, after successful migration and API deployment gates, may update the `develop` Pages alias/custom domains.
- Add workflow contract tests for an ordinary feature PR and a `develop → main` release PR, proving neither can target `main` or `develop`.
- Preserve the post-deploy routing/commit check for canonical releases; previews must remain isolated from custom staging domains.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

N/A - this is a deployment-isolation defect. The authoritative proof is the exact GitHub Actions job output plus the two live JSON build stamps below.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- [ ] MP4 recording or JPG screenshots of the broken behavior. N/A - no visual assertion is needed for the branch collision.
- [x] Backend/deployment logs. The linked exact run records `PR_HEAD_REF: develop`, `PAGES_BRANCH: develop`, both successful Pages aliases, and skipped migration/API jobs.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectory. N/A - no model behavior is involved.
- [x] Domain artifacts. At 2026-08-08 21:27 UTC, `app-staging.elizacloud.ai/eliza-renderer-build.json` reported frontend commit `3e10652a25571a94b61c9ce3646bc358f7ade7ed`, a synthetic merge of production base `5ca304dd288a8529ec566a9567c4576a48cafafa` and `develop@ba0dc76f86561ba1642255193ab1217b2b013e8b`; `api-staging.elizacloud.ai/api/health` still reported `55eb734eda5f3650d5c3a4b7da0e671d5c35436a`.

**Additional context**

The workflow comments say PRs deploy to a preview branch, and the routing job skips PRs because previews are assumed to use an isolated alias. That assumption is false for the release PR because its real head ref is the canonical `develop` branch. The Pages freshness verifier also skips pull-request events, so this overwrite can complete green without detecting the staging frontend/API skew.

Cross-link this with the ongoing staging QA/provisioning work because it invalidates claims made against a supposedly single staging release, but the deploy isolation bug is independently reproducible without authentication or state mutation.

topPRs.title: fix(ui): require verified OAuth markers on /auth/success
topPRs.author: wtfsayo
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #18054.

Anonymous navigation to `/auth/success` no longer renders a trusted "Connected" card from query parameters alone.

**Verification contract (this head `084b5512549b7d1a632dc00c8b8d786bfb199035`):**

1. Query parsing yields only a *candidate* (`resolveAuthSuccessCandidate`). Known-provider `*_connected` markers or `connection_id` alone never claim success.
2. Success requires **one** of:
   - A **callback-minted short-lived HMAC proof** verified by public `GET /api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify?proof=…` (covers Twitter/Discord and sessionless API-key OAuth returns to `/auth/success`), and when a `connection_id` is present a sessioned browser must also own that connection; or
   - An **authenticated ownership lookup** `GET /api/v1/oauth/connections/:id` returning an active connection for the current org/user (sessioned browsers without a proof).
3. Until verification succeeds the page stays **pending**, then **verified**, **unverified**, or **unavailable** (distinct UI for transport/5xx).

**Backend changes:**

- `mintOAuthSuccessProof` / `verifyOAuthSuccessProof` (HMAC, ~10 min TTL, nonce) in cloud shared OAuth services
- Generic OAuth2, Twitter (OAuth1a + OAuth2), and Discord callbacks attach `proof` only when the redirect path is exactly `/auth/success`
- Public path allowlist for `/api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify`
- Reserved markers (`proof`, `platform`, `connection_id`, known `*_connected`) are cleared before rewriting so a prior success URL cannot retain a valid proof across an error redirect

**Provider contracts preserved:**

| Callback | Success query shape on `/auth/success` |
| --- | --- |
| Generic OAuth2 | `{platform}_connected=true&platform=…&connection_id=…&proof=…` |
| Twitter | `twitter_connected=true&platform=twitter&proof=…` (no connection_id) |
| Discord | `discord=connected&platform=discord&discord_connected=true&proof=…` |

Forged marker-only URLs stay **unverified**.

- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared test src/lib/services/oauth/success-proof.test.ts` → **7 passed**
- [x] Focused classifier coverage: forged known-provider markers rejected; Twitter/Discord proof candidates accepted; ownership 404/403 rejected; 503 → unavailable

# Risks

**Medium.** Plugin load set and connect-handoff routing for lean-chat Calendar /
Google Workspace. Mis-gating could load Node-only Workspace on mobile or leave
owners without a working setup card. Mitigations: mobile filter last, OAuth trio
alignment, `enabled:false` final delete, trusted OAuth URL allowlist, CONFIG ids
matched to `/api/plugins`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Makes lean-chat Google Calendar connect/sync **workable and safe**:

1. **Scheduling** — Seeded in lean-chat because Calendar is already always selected and hard-depends on it.
2. **Google Workspace (gated)** — Loads only on explicit Google signals (entries enable, configured googlechat, or full `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`+`SECRET`+`REDIRECT_URI`). Empty `{}` googlechat does **not** load. **`enabled: false` is a final deny**.
3. **Mobile order** — Companion adds run **before** the mobile allow-list so Workspace cannot re-enter iOS/Android load sets.
4. **Trusted OAuth URLs only** — Verified handoffs require known Google/Microsoft authorize hosts/paths; untrusted hosts refused.

# Risks

Medium-low. This changes the final request-construction boundary for OpenAI and Anthropic and the copy-on-write semantics of the shared sanitizer. The principal risk was breaking AI SDK identity/callback metadata while cleaning wire-visible strings; descriptor and prototype regressions now cover that explicitly.

# Background

The previous sanitizer closed the mid-emoji prompt failure but left several related gaps:

1. malformed object keys, structured-output schemas, tool metadata, provider options, and Anthropic stop sequences could still reach provider JSON;
2. surrogate-safe truncation markers counted requested rather than actually retained UTF-16 units;
3. the first copy-on-write follow-up cleaned wire bytes but could drop non-enumerable SDK callbacks, alter symbol descriptors, or change the source prototype.

This head fixes the entire boundary:

- sanitizes enumerable JSON keys and values recursively with collision-safe `__proto__` handling;
- sanitizes plain response schemas before AI SDK wrappers create promise-backed response formats;
- sanitizes OpenAI and Anthropic tools, tool choice, provider options, output schemas, and stop sequences;
- preserves SDK functions, accessors, symbol/non-enumerable descriptors, and Object/null prototypes during copy-on-write;
- computes truncation counts from actual retained head/tail lengths.

No UI or user-facing documentation changes.

- OpenAI wire suite: **5/5 pass**

## What

Fixes two defects exposed by a live owner test of character modification (2026-08-08, Discord deployment; sanitized trajectories attached).

### 1 — CHARACTER.modify died on a single classifier flake

Live: the owner asked for a character change; the planner routed `CHARACTER_MODIFY` with `request: "add a strict rule to my personality: never say 'bet' under any circumstances."`; `detectModificationIntent` threw `ElizaError: Failed to classify character modification intent` (character.ts:1080) and the whole action failed with a generic glitch line. Root cause: that request shape slipped past the rule heuristic's definitive branch ("add" was not a change verb, "never say X" was not a recognized speech rule), fell to the ONE strict-JSON `TEXT_SMALL` call, and the deployment's small model flaked on it — one bad parse killed the action closed.

Structural fixes in `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/personality/actions/character.ts`:

- **Rule fast path covers the live shapes.** `detectModificationIntentByRules` now classifies definitively, with no model round-trip: speech-rule imperatives (`never say X`, `stop saying X`, `don't say X`), additive asks (`add a rule to my personality: ...`, `remove X from your topics`), and degree directives (`be more X`, `act less X`). The exact live request and the exact raw owner message both hit the fast path.
- **Tolerant parsing + one reroll on the model path.** `parseStructuredRecord` now uses `parseJsonObject` (the same recovery layer as `runtime/validated-model-call.ts`: fenced/prose-wrapped/embedded objects recovered, never a fake-valid default), and the intent call rerolls once on an invalid response — mirroring validated-model-call's remote reroll, capped at one because the heuristic already resolves every unambiguous shape. The tolerant parser also hardens the parse/safety/identity call sites that share the helper.
- **Actionable failure surface.** If classification still fails after the reroll, the planner-facing result says what phrasing works (`ask them to rephrase it concretely, like "change your personality to ..."`) instead of the generic unexpected-error line, with `errorType: intent_classification_failed`.

### 2 — owner-gated character asks from non-owners were silently ignored

Live: a GUEST-role sender issued the same command directly. Role gating correctly excludes `CHARACTER` (roleGate ADMIN floor) from the planner surface — but the turn ended Stage-1-only with the reply "on it." and zero planner iterations. The sender was promised a change that silently never ran, with no indication it was a permissions matter.

Structural fix, following the existing gate-feedback pattern (`ownerExclusiveSuppressionNote` in `security/trusted-delivery-audience.ts` — context in, model out, no hardcoded reply strings):

- **New `CHARACTER_GATE_NOTICE` provider** (`personality/providers/character-gate-notice.ts`, registered in `advancedProviders`, `alwaysInResponseState` so it reaches Stage 1 even when role filtering strips the settings context for exactly these senders). When the deterministic rule classifier marks the current message as a definitive character-modification ask AND the sender fails the CHARACTER action's effective role gate (ACTION_ROLE_POLICY override honored — a deployment that loosens the gate never emits a false refusal hint), it injects a model-visible notice: the capability is role-gated, do not promise or imply the change, decline in your own voice. The model phrases the refusal; no reply string is hardcoded.

### 3 — routing double-claim (one-liner)

Live startup warning: `simile claimed by multiple parents — dropped from routing as ambiguous (simile=UPDATE_OWNER_NAME, parents=["CHARACTER","SETTINGS"])`. `UPDATE_OWNER_NAME` names the owner's profile name — SETTINGS territory (`packages/agent/src/actions/settings-actions.ts` claims it; the provider-context catalog maps it to `settings`). Dropped the stale claim from CHARACTER's similes so the simile routes again.

## Tests

`packages/core/.../personality/__tests__/character-modify-intent.test.ts` (17) and `character-gate-notice.test.ts` (5), real handlers/provider against the in-memory FakeRuntime, real `hasRoleAccess`, scripted model stubs:

|---|---|
| Rule fast path: exact live planner request, exact raw owner message (bare + mention-prefixed), `never say X`, `stop saying X`, `don't say X`, `be more/less X`, `act more X` → definitive explicit | pass |
| Unrelated text → definitive non-request; ambiguous character talk → inconclusive (model path) | pass |
| Fast path end-to-end: live request applies with zero intent-classifier calls (parse + safety only) | pass |
| Model path: flaky-then-valid → one reroll, valid retry used | pass |
| Model path: fenced JSON accepted on first attempt (tolerant parse) | pass |
| Still-invalid after reroll → `intent_classification_failed` + actionable phrasing guidance | pass |
| GUEST explicit ask → gate notice with required role; owner identical ask → no notice; unrelated/ambiguous GUEST messages → no notice; `ACTION_ROLE_POLICY` loosened to GUEST → no notice | pass |
